description: Create report_generator.py - Professional Bug Bounty Report Generator with CVSS 3.1 calculator, HackerOne-format reports, and multiple output formats (JSON, Markdown, HTML). Also create main.py - the Master Controller that orchestrates all modules, handles CLI arguments, provides real-time progress, manages concurrency, and produces combined output.
steps: Implement CVSS 3.1 vector calculator: take attack vector (Network/Adjacent/Local/Physical), attack complexity (Low/High), privileges required (None/Low/High), user interaction (None/Required), scope (Unchanged/Changed), and CIA impact (None/Low/High) - compute base score per CVSS 3.1 formula
Implement severity classification: map CVSS scores to Critical (9.0-10.0), High (7.0-8.9), Medium (4.0-6.9), Low (0.1-3.9), Info (0.0)

Implement HackerOne report template generator: for each finding, produce title, severity, CVSS vector + score, vulnerability type, description (what was found), impact (what an attacker could do), steps to reproduce (PoC template), remediation recommendation, references (CWE link, OWASP reference)
Implement executive summary generator: total findings by severity, most critical issues, overall security posture assessment, prioritized remediation roadmap
Implement JSON output: structured data with all findings, metadata (scan time, target, modules used), statistics
Implement Markdown output: formatted report with table of contents, severity badges, findings organized by module and severity

Implement HTML output: dark-themed report with CSS styling, collapsible sections, severity color coding (red/orange/yellow/blue/gray), statistics bar chart (CSS-only), navigation sidebar, print-friendly styles
Implement statistics dashboard: findings count by severity, by type, by target, scan duration, modules executed
Create /projects/sandbox/Bug-Bounty/monster/main.py with a Monster class as master controller

Implement CLI argument parsing in main.py: --scope (file with domains), --target (single domain), --apk (APK file path to extract URLs from), --module (recon/js/vuln/report/all), --output/-o (output directory), --threads (thread count), --rate-limit (delay between requests), --timeout, --dry-run, --verbose, --no-color, --resume (skip already-scanned), --config (custom config file path)
Implement APK integration: if --apk provided, run the existing apk_analyzer/analyze.py to extract URLs/domains, then feed them into the monster pipeline

Implement orchestration flow: (1) parse scope/targets, (2) run recon module, (3) run js_analyzer on discovered URLs, (4) run vuln_scanner with all collected data, (5) run report_generator to produce output
Implement real-time progress display with colored output: [MONSTER] banner, module headers, per-target progress with finding counts, spinner/progress indicators using simple ASCII animation

Implement output directory structure: results/{target}/recon.json, results/{target}/js_analysis.json, results/{target}/vulnerabilities.json, results/report.json, results/report.md, results/report.html, results/findings/ (individual HackerOne reports)
Implement resume capability: check if results/{target}/module.json already exists, skip if --resume flag is set
Implement rate limiting controls: global rate limiter shared across all threads
Implement concurrent scanning: use ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel subdomain resolution and multi-target scanning, with configurable thread count
Add connectivity check at startup: verify network access before starting scan
acceptance_criteria: python -m monster --help shows all CLI options with descriptions
python -m monster --target example.com --module recon --dry-run -o /tmp/monster-test runs without error
ReportGenerator produces valid HTML with dark theme and severity badges
ReportGenerator produces valid Markdown with proper formatting
CVSS calculator produces correct scores for known vectors
Main controller properly orchestrates modules in sequence
Resume flag correctly skips already-completed targets
Rate limiting is applied across all network operations

python -c "from monster.main import Monster; print('main import OK')"
